source_snapshot.test_name_items: SOL console - in BIOS setup menu and output BIOS log , keyboard type check
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    *Before using SOL consoles, the user must execute the IPMI OEM command - "Set SOL Enable" to enable the SOL consoles. If default setting is enable at your project, you don't need to proceed this step.

1. Click "Operations" -> " SOL console" in BMC WebUI page.
2. Power on SUT and enter to BIOS setup menu.
3. check the console screen and the keyboard function.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. SOL console should show the log info during boot up, also can see the BIOS setup screen.
2. Keyboard should type in any key and respond correctly.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- not runnable by agent: the "SOL console in BIOS setup menu" check requires opening an SOL serial-console session into the BIOS setup screen and reading the BIOS menu/log output; the agent cannot render/interact with the BIOS setup UI through SOL over plain SSH.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO correctly recognizes that plain host SSH cannot prove BIOS-stage SOL rendering or keyboard behavior, but it overstates the manual boundary: an approved SOL client can automate transcript capture and safe key injection once the platform-specific enablement, serial channel and human visual checkpoints are defined.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY / IMPROVED adds target identity, approved OEM enablement, safe keyboard interaction and cleanup. V3.1 reclassifies the case as a package-and-confirmation workflow because protocol-level SOL capture and bounded input can be automated while WebUI path, BIOS visual interpretation, power action and verdict remain human-controlled.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 909/2291 retains NO/physical status and generic operator photos, but does not distinguish WebUI coverage from an alternate SOL client, define OEM enable bytes, UART parameters, BIOS-redirection readiness, safe key matrix or restoration of a temporary SOL setting.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: The immediately following OS-condition SOL case has separate bootloader/OS-console configuration and cannot prove BIOS POST/setup coverage. Generic KVM or host SSH output is not equivalent to SOL BIOS-stage evidence.

historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this exact case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the source WebUI path and OEM enable requirement; ED-34 treats Project SOL parameters and approved power window as readiness inputs; ED-35 prevents reducing BIOS-stage functional input to passive host-log inspection; ED-38 requires explicit point-of-action approval, no automatic retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify the BMC WebUI SOL console for the intended SUT carries attributable BIOS boot/POST output, displays the BIOS setup menu and correctly transports a bounded set of safe keyboard inputs without changing BIOS configuration.
original_method: Confirm or enable SOL only through the Project-approved vendor method, open Operations > SOL console in the BMC WebUI, perform one approved host power-on/boot, enter BIOS setup, capture the BIOS-stage stream and exercise harmless navigation keys, then exit without saving, close the session and restore any temporary SOL setting.
manual_activity: An engineer approves the SOL enable method, serial configuration, one host boot/power action and harmless key matrix. A human opens or visually verifies the source-specified WebUI console, confirms BIOS menu rendering and ensures exit without save. Automation may capture the serial stream, correlate markers and inject only pre-approved keys, but cannot authorize power/BIOS actions or issue the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT identity, BMC and BIOS versions, host power state and independent observation/recovery path
Current SOL enable state and exact vendor-supported enable/readback/restore command or WebUI control; no guessed OEM bytes
SOL channel/payload instance, authentication privilege, UART parameters, terminal type/encoding and BIOS serial-redirection map
Supported WebUI/browser or alternative SOL client version, account/role and audit/session behavior
Approved maintenance and power-on/boot window plus BIOS entry timing and expected POST/setup markers
Safe keyboard matrix such as arrows, Tab and Esc, with expected focus/navigation, latency and no-drop criteria
Exit-without-save, session close, temporary-SOL restore and final host-state recovery plan
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, BMC audit, SOL, boot or host logs; preserve the baseline and first-failure evidence.
Verify BMC/SUT identity and current host power state before opening SOL or presenting a power action; do not use reset, power-cycle or automatic retry as a substitute.
Do not guess the IPMI OEM command, channel, payload instance, privilege or serial parameters. Record and use only a vendor/Project-approved method.
Do not save BIOS changes, alter boot order, firmware, security, password, storage or platform settings. Limit input to the approved harmless navigation matrix.
If the session points to the wrong target, output is garbled, keys repeat/drop, BIOS state is uncertain or the host does not follow the approved boot path, stop input and preserve evidence.
Exit BIOS without saving, close SOL, restore only a temporary approved SOL state and verify the final host/BMC state through an independent path.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the identity, approved SOL method/parameters, BIOS redirection, evidence markers, power window, safe-key and recovery contracts; present any state-changing action for explicit confirmation.

After approval and human WebUI interaction or an approved equivalent client, capture the timestamped SOL transcript and correlate boot/POST and BIOS-setup markers without substituting host SSH output.
Inject only approved harmless navigation keys when the client supports controlled automation, record sent/received timing and retain human visual confirmation of focus/navigation and rendering.
Archive raw/redacted evidence, compare final state and stop without log clearing, BIOS save, guessed OEM action, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the exact SOL enable/readback/restore mechanism, serial channel/UART settings, WebUI/client coverage and one host boot/power action.
Define BIOS markers, harmless key-response matrix, latency/drop/garble criteria, abort conditions and exit/recovery behavior.
Supervise the BIOS-stage visual checkpoint and power/BIOS boundary, review evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its no-command conclusion fits plain SSH, but not every approved execution environment. SOL is a protocol that can support automated capture and bounded input; those capabilities do not eliminate the source WebUI and human BIOS-visual checkpoints.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the Project-approved WebUI SOL flow. An approved vendor client or IPMI SOL utility may provide capture/input automation only with exact channel, payload, privilege and serial parameters; document it as a Project Override and retain the uncovered WebUI coverage.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source WebUI path, conditional OEM `Set SOL Enable`, host power-on, BIOS entry, boot-log/menu and keyboard Criteria, no Script, DeepSeek NO text and 5/5-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not invent OEM bytes or accept arbitrary `any key`.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Baseline SOL and BIOS redirection, use the approved WebUI path for one authorized boot, capture the BIOS-stage stream and verify a harmless key matrix with human visual confirmation, then exit without saving and restore temporary state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC WebUI/SOL implementation, BIOS serial-redirection implementation and approved SUT management path.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware/WebUI build, BIOS build, browser or SOL-client version and UART/channel configuration.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: BMC vendor SOL/OEM command manual, BIOS serial-redirection specification, Project power/maintenance plan and recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes conditional enablement, serial identity, safe keyboard semantics, evidence and restoration explicit without changing the source WebUI/BIOS purpose.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A CLI/vendor SOL client can validate transport, capture and input but not automatically prove the BMC WebUI console path; passive boot logs do not prove keyboard control or BIOS menu rendering.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Approved enablement and serial parameters, platform identity, WebUI/client, boot window, BIOS markers, safe key matrix and recovery plan.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong-target SOL or BIOS input can affect boot/configuration; mismatched UART settings can garble evidence; BMC reset or power retry can disrupt the SUT.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use an approved IPMI SOL or vendor serial client for protocol capture and safe key injection if the original WebUI method, actual client, reason, engineering approval and equivalent transport/input checkpoints are recorded. Passing the override does not claim the WebUI SOL page itself passed, and host SSH or post-boot logs are only partial evidence.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT identity, BMC/BIOS/client versions, host power baseline, SOL enable state/method and complete channel/UART/BIOS-redirection configuration
Approval for the WebUI session and one boot/power action, with redacted login/session/audit timestamps and independent host observation
Raw timestamped SOL capture showing attributable POST/boot markers and BIOS setup, plus screenshots proving source WebUI rendering when that path is required
Per-key matrix with transmitted harmless key, visible navigation/focus response, latency, repeated/dropped/garbled characters and human confirmation
Exit-without-save and session-close proof, restored temporary SOL state, final host/BMC/BIOS state, preserved logs, coverage differences and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title, Procedure and Criteria consistently require BMC WebUI SOL at BIOS stage with boot output, BIOS setup visibility and keyboard response. Missing OEM bytes, serial parameters and a bounded safe-key definition are execution-readiness gaps, not contradictory core semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The SOL BIOS-stage purpose and source method are clear. Project/vendor inputs can define enablement, serial settings, power approval, expected markers and recovery, so missing inputs do not make the review permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes blanket NO to PACKAGE because approved SOL tooling can automate capture and bounded input, while preserving the human WebUI/BIOS/power boundary and rejecting plain SSH substitution.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Strengthens its safe manual controls and reclassifies only the automatable protocol/evidence portion; human confirmation and source WebUI coverage remain mandatory.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic physical photos with attributable BIOS-stage transcript, WebUI screenshots, exact session/serial configuration, per-key evidence and reversible enablement.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps OS-console SOL, KVM and host-SSH evidence outside this BIOS/WebUI verdict.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents plain host output, a generic SOL connection or uncontrolled `any key` from being reported as proof of the source WebUI BIOS console, while preserving useful automation for transcript capture and bounded input under explicit approval.
independent_technical_reasoning: SOL transports a serial payload and can be driven programmatically, but coverage depends on a platform-specific payload/channel/UART configuration and BIOS redirection. The source separately requires the BMC WebUI presentation and BIOS-stage visual state. Therefore the correct boundary is a hybrid package: automate protocol capture and approved keys where possible, retain human confirmation for WebUI rendering and BIOS navigation, and never equate host SSH or passive logs with full coverage.
